lead: From El Cabanyal to La Devesa, from Spain’s liveliest promenade to the virgin dunes of the Albufera Natural Park. Valencia’s coastline has a beach for every style.

Valencia is one of the few big cities in the world where you can go to the beach by metro. The beaches of El Cabanyal, La Malvarrosa and La Patacona form a continuous seafront of more than three kilometres of golden sand with a promenade, restaurants and all services, barely 20 minutes from the historic centre. To the south, the natural beaches of the Albufera Natural Park — El Saler, Garrofera, La Devesa — offer a radical change: dunes, pine forests and kilometres of almost unspoilt coastline.

All of the city’s beaches hold the Blue Flag, which guarantees water quality and services. And thanks to the more than 300 days of sun a year of Valencia’s Mediterranean climate, they can be enjoyed all year round.

items.title: Cabanyal Beach · Las Arenas
items.subtitle: Next to the seafaring Cabanyal district · Next to the Marina · It inspired Sorolla
items.body: Cabanyal beach, also called Las Arenas, is the closest to the Marina Real Juan Carlos I and one of the city’s most emblematic. At 1.2 kilometres long and up to 200 metres wide, it is the widest urban beach in Valencia. Located next to the historic seafaring district of El Cabanyal, it was the beach that inspired the painter Joaquín Sorolla in many of his seafaring works. Opposite it stands the former Hotel Balneario Las Arenas, which in the 20s–40s was the city’s fashionable spa and is now a luxury hotel. The promenade that runs along it connects directly with the Paseo Neptuno and La Malvarrosa.

items.kicker: Urban beach · The most popular in Valencia · 1.8 km
items.title: Malvarrosa Beach
items.subtitle: The great promenade · La Pepica · La Marcelina · Casa Carmela
items.body: La Malvarrosa is Valencia’s most emblematic and most visited beach. With 1.8 kilometres of golden sand and a width of 135 metres, it offers space for everyone. Its promenade, lively all year round, is flanked by palm trees and has some of the city’s most traditional restaurants: La Pepica and La Marcelina, both open for more than a century, are institutions of seaside Valencian paella. The writer Blasco Ibáñez lived next to this beach, and the House Museum where he lived is preserved at its northern end. The Oceanogràfic pumps its seawater directly from this beach. It holds the Q for Tourism Quality, the Qualitur and the accessibility certification.

items.kicker: Urban beach · Alboraya · Quiet atmosphere · 1+ km
items.title: La Patacona Beach
items.subtitle: Horchata from the huerta · Relaxed atmosphere · Horses at sunrise
items.body: La Patacona is the natural continuation of La Malvarrosa to the north, belonging to the municipality of Alboraya — the world capital of horchata. At more than a kilometre long and 100 metres wide, it keeps a somewhat quieter atmosphere than its neighbours, especially on weekdays. First thing in the morning and at sunset, riders from a nearby equestrian centre take their horses along the shoreline, creating a unique postcard image. Its promenade has a good range of bars, ice-cream shops, restaurants and beach bars that organise concerts at sunset in summer. Two minutes from the beach, the Valencian huerta has the best authentic horchata shops.

items.kicker: Natural beach · Albufera Natural Park · 5 km
items.title: El Saler Beach
items.subtitle: Dunes · Pine forests · Blue Flag · Windsurfing and kitesurfing
items.body: El Saler beach is the jewel of the Valencian coast and a complete change of landscape from the urban beaches. Located within the Albufera Natural Park — just 15 minutes by car from the centre — its 5 kilometres of fine golden sand are surrounded by natural dunes and Mediterranean pine forests that act as a windbreak. The protected setting and the wind conditions make it especially popular with windsurfing and kitesurfing fans. It has the Blue Flag and all the essential services: lifeguards, showers, toilets, restaurants and a cycle lane that crosses the dunes. For nature lovers it is a unique experience.

items.title: Pinedo Beach
items.subtitle: Fishing and farming village · Huerta setting
items.body: Pinedo beach is one of the best options for escaping the hustle and bustle without going too far from the city. At more than a kilometre and a half long, it offers a quiet setting next to the picturesque village of Pinedo, a former fishing and farming enclave that has become a tourist attraction in recent years. Its width of barely 32 metres and its local atmosphere make it ideal for those looking for a beach without crowds. Between Pinedo and El Saler lies the Arbre del Gos beach, one of the most unspoilt in the city, 2.6 kilometres long in the heart of the Albufera setting.

items.title: La Devesa Beach
items.subtitle: The most natural in Valencia · Pine forests · Dunes · Protected wildlife
items.body: La Devesa is the wildest beach in Valencia and one of the most unique experiences on the Spanish Mediterranean coast. Almost 5 kilometres long, it lies between the Mediterranean and the Albufera lake — one of the largest freshwater lakes in Spain. The surrounding ecosystem includes pine forests, dwarf fan palms, kermes oaks, mastic trees and a dune system of great ecological value where dozens of species of birds can be seen. The area connecting with El Saler beach is used by naturists. It has the Blue Flag and lifeguard services, showers and toilets, along with an Albufera Natural Park information point and a wildlife observatory.

blocks.title: Tips for enjoying Valencia’s beaches
items: Go by metro or bus: the L4 drops you at Les Arenes and bus 19 reaches La Malvarrosa with no parking hassle
Paella by the sea at La Pepica or Casa Carmela is a priceless experience — book ahead in summer
If you are looking for peace and quiet, choose La Patacona on weekdays or El Saler instead of La Malvarrosa in August
El Saler beach is only 15 min by car: virgin dunes, pine forests and the Albufera in the background
The cycle lane connects the Marina with La Patacona along the promenade: a flat 8 km route beside the sea
At La Patacona first thing: the horses from the equestrian centre walk along the shoreline at sunrise — do not miss it
